name: LTIMindtree
summary: LTIMindtree, the Larsen & Toubro group's technology services company, introduced the brand name LTM in 2026. It hires freshers mainly through campus and off-campus drives that candidates commonly describe as an online assessment of aptitude, reasoning and coding, then technical and HR interviews. It publishes four values: Driven by purpose, Act with compassion, Be future-ready and Deliver impact.
rounds: Campus drive, off-campus registration or online application
Online assessment: aptitude, reasoning, English and coding (often)
Technical interview on fundamentals, your coding approach and your projects
For experienced roles: one or two technical rounds, then a manager discussion
looks_for: Data, cloud or AI basics for newer roles
A clear explanation of your own projects

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and the project you're proudest of.
covers: Your degree or experience and your strongest skills, briefly
The project: the problem, your part and one result
Why this role is the right next step

questions.text: Tell me about a time you kept going on something because you believed in why it mattered.
covers: What the goal was and why it mattered to you or others
The setback that could have made you stop
What kept you going and what you achieved

questions.text: Tell me about a time you noticed someone on your team was having a hard time. What did you do?
covers: What you noticed and how you raised it kindly
The practical help you gave, without taking over
How it changed things for them and the team

questions.text: Tell me about something new you taught yourself because you expected to need it.
covers: Why you saw the need coming
How you learned it and how you practised
Where you've used it since

questions.text: Tell me about a result you delivered that someone else could measure.
covers: The goal and who cared about it
What you did to get there
The result as a number or a clear before-and-after

questions.text: Explain the difference between an array and a linked list, and when you'd choose each.
covers: Array: items side by side in memory, fast access by index, costly inserts in the middle
Linked list: nodes with pointers, cheap inserts and deletes, slow access by position
A use case for each

questions.text: What is an index in a database, and when can adding one make things slower?
covers: An index works like a book's index: finding rows without reading the whole table
It speeds up reads and filters on the indexed columns
It slows down inserts and updates and takes space, so too many hurt

questions.text: How would you design a simple link-shortening service: what would you store, and how would lookups work?
covers: Clarifying scale and features, such as custom links or expiry
Storing short code to long URL, and how codes are generated without clashes
Fast redirects using an index or cache, and counting clicks

questions.text: What is the difference between Git merge and rebase, and why do teams use pull requests?
covers: Merge joins histories with a merge commit; rebase replays your commits on top of another branch
Why not to rebase shared branches
Pull requests for review, tests and a record of changes

questions.text: What does a REST API do, and what do the common HTTP methods mean?
covers: An API that exposes resources at URLs and exchanges data, often JSON
GET, POST, PUT or PATCH and DELETE, each in a line
Status codes such as 200, 201, 400, 404 and 500

questions.text: Your code passes on your machine but fails in the build pipeline. What do you check?
covers: Differences in versions, environment variables or missing files
Tests that depend on order, time or local data
Reading the pipeline log carefully and reproducing it in a clean setup

questions.text: For experienced candidates: tell me about a time you improved the performance of something in production. How did you measure it?
covers: The slow part and how users or the business felt it
How you found the bottleneck, with the numbers before and after
Any trade-off the fix brought

questions.text: Why LTIMindtree, and what do you know about the industries it works in?
covers: Something specific you've read on its site or in recent news
One industry or service line that interests you and why
How it fits your skills and plans

questions.text: What would you like to be working on two years from now?
covers: A realistic direction, such as a technology, a domain or a bigger role in a team
The skills you'll build to get there
How this role starts you on that path

tips: The company introduced the brand LTM in 2026, so you may see both names on job posts and emails; either is fine in an interview.
Practise coding in timed conditions in one language, and explain your approach before you write code.
Prepare a short story for each published value; 'Be future-ready' and 'Deliver impact' suit learning and project stories.
Read a recent case study or press release in an industry you like, so 'why us' sounds specific.

sources.title: LTIMindtree introduces new brand identity as LTM (ltm.com)

rounds: Manager or client interview (for many roles)
